TSL Learning 03: Conditionals (If/Else)

GPU shaders need conditionals too! TSL provides If, ElseIf, and Else that look different from JavaScript but work similarly.

Syntax Comparison

JavaScript TSL 
if (x > 5) {
    result = 1;
}
 
If(x.greaterThan(5), () => {
    result.assign(1);
});
 
if (x > 5) {
    result = 1;
} else {
    result = 0;
}
 
If(x.greaterThan(5), () => {
    result.assign(1);
}).Else(() => {
    result.assign(0);
});
 
if (x > 5) {
    result = 2;
} else if (x > 0) {
    result = 1;
} else {
    result = 0;
}
 
If(x.greaterThan(5), () => {
    result.assign(2);
}).ElseIf(x.greaterThan(0), () => {
    result.assign(1);
}).Else(() => {
    result.assign(0);
});

Comparison Operators

JavaScript TSL
a > ba.greaterThan(b)
a >= ba.greaterThanEqual(b)
a < ba.lessThan(b)
a <= ba.lessThanEqual(b)
a === ba.equal(b)
a !== ba.notEqual(b)
a && ba.and(b)
a || ba.or(b)
!aa.not()

Example: Classify Numbers

Let's classify numbers as negative (-1), zero (0), or positive (1).

Click "Run Example" to see the result...

The Code

import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';
import { Fn, If, instancedArray, instanceIndex, float } from 'three/tsl';

// Initialize WebGPU
const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer();
await renderer.init();

// Input data
const inputData = new Float32Array([-5, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 5, -100, 100]);
const inputBuffer = instancedArray(inputData, 'float');

// Output buffer
const outputBuffer = instancedArray(new Float32Array(inputData.length), 'float');

// Classify: negative → -1, zero → 0, positive → 1
const classifyKernel = Fn(() => {
    const value = inputBuffer.element(instanceIndex);
    const result = float(0);

    If(value.lessThan(0), () => {
        result.assign(-1);
    }).ElseIf(value.greaterThan(0), () => {
        result.assign(1);
    });
    // If value === 0, result stays 0

    outputBuffer.element(instanceIndex).assign(result);
})().compute(inputData.length);

// Execute
await renderer.computeAsync(classifyKernel);

// Read results
const gpuBuffer = await renderer.getArrayBufferAsync(outputBuffer.value);
const results = new Float32Array(gpuBuffer);
console.log(results); // [-1, -1, 0, 1, 1, -1, 1]

Optional: toVar()

The .toVar() function is optional in most cases. TSL handles assignment automatically. Use .toVar('name') when you want to give a variable a specific name in the generated shader: 

// Both of these work for assignment:
const x = float(5);
const y = float(5).toVar();

x.assign(10);  // Works!
y.assign(10);  // Also works!

// Use toVar('name') for debugging (names the variable in the shader)
const depth = sampleDepth(uv).toVar('depth');
